title.narrative: Marie Stopes International 2019-2025 - Marie Stopes International 2019-2022

description.narrative: Insatsen fokuserar på mödra- och barn hälsovård genom att bland annat öka tillgången på preventivmedel, öka förståelsen och acceptansen för familjeplanering. Marie Stopes International tillhandahåller dessutom basal barn- och mödrahälsovård och ger psykosocialt stöd till kvinnor som utsatts för våld i hemmet. Under 2023 nådde Sidas stöd 103 596 kvinnor och flickor i Afghanistan med information, utbildning och service kring sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa.

Marie Stopes International Afghanistan (MSIA) has submitted an application for support for the period 2019-2021, with a budget amounting to USD 4 145 610. Sida has been giving project support to MSIA since 2012; the planned support will be the fourth phase of their Afghanistan programme. MSIA works with sexual and reproductive health and rights raising awareness and increasing access for women to affordable services and products preventing unintended pregnancies and maternal deaths. Although the main beneficiaries are women, MSIA's outreach activities include also adolescents and men. The organisation is present in 11 provinces, of which Sida is presently funding activities in three provinces outside of Kabul - in Balkh, Jowzjan and Herat. The application aims at extending the project to include districts in three more provinces in Helmand, Kandahar and Nangarhar. These provinces in southern and eastern Afghanistan are contested and access to them subsequently requires functioning relations with the local Taliban leadership. The human rights situation in Afghanistan remains poor, especially in rural areas, and maternal mortality is among the highest in the world, driven by low availability of skilled SRH care and early and frequent pregnancies. In 2015, the WHO reported the Maternal Mortality Rate in Afghanistan to be 396 per 100 000 live births. This might be an underestimation because of lack of reliable information. As a comparison, the Sustainable Development Goal 3.1 is to reduce the global maternal mortality ratio by 2030 to less than 70 per 100 000 live births. The national modern contraceptive prevalence is low as well; only one in five women uses a modern contraception method. According to information from MSIA the prevalence among adolescents (15-19 years) could be as low as 6% even though 45% of respondents were married.Mode of operation:At the national level, MSIA cooperates with relevant ministries and finances three advisers/consultants to promote the inclusion of SRHR in their policies. The Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) has included SRH in the standard Basic Package of Health Services (BPHS), although still in a limited way. Cooperation with the Ministry of Education promotes the introduction of SRH in the curriculum. Cooperation with the Ministries of Women's Affairs and Religious Affairs promotes the acceptance of SRH among the general population.At the provincial level, MSIA works out of static clinics offering a full range of services such as contraception, STI and HIV testing, child health services, immunization, as well as post- and ante-natal care, together with laboratory services. MSIA also works out of satellite clinics, usually hospitals, governmental health clinics, or other organisations. They are e.g. in the process of signing a Memorandum of Understanding with Médecins Sans Fontières for partnership, where MSF refers postnatal care and contraception services, and MSIA refers women to MSF for safe delivery services.At local level, one of MSIA’s strengths is the mobile clinics with skilled community health workers (CHW) who provide services and information to the rural, and often very poor, population.A service added to the application following the evaluation is psychosocial counselling of survivors of violence in prison. A consequence of harmful practices has been that a significant part of the female prison population consists of girls who have run away from forced marriages, domestic violence or who fail a virginity test end up with prison sentences. MSI plans to make SRH part of the psychosocial counselling services. The relevant National Priority Program in line with the Afghan National Peace and Development Framework (ANPDF) is the NPP for Human Capital, which includes universal and quality health care services, designed for 2019-2023 and to be financed through the World Bank administered Trust Fund ARTF.

tag.narrative: 3.7 - By 2030, ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health-care services, including for family planning, information and education, and the integration of reproductive health into national strategies and programmes.

3.7 - Senast 2030 säkerställa att alla har tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsovård, inklusive familjeplanering, information och utbildning, och att reproduktiv hälsa integreras i nationella strategier och program.

5.6 - Ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights as agreed in accordance with the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development and the Beijing Platform for Action and the outcome documents of their review conferences.

5.6 - Säkerställa allmän tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och reproduktiva rättigheter i enlighet med överenskommelserna i handlingsprogrammet från den internationella konferensen om befolkning och utveckling, Pekingplattformen samt slutdokumenten från respektive översynskonferenser.
